The function has been effective at launching products; what it has not yet built is the strategic layer that comes after launch – the continuous positioning, adoption strategy, and market intelligence that makes each product more valuable over time. This role owns that shift.</p> <p>The Director of Product Marketing and Market Research is a combined senior leadership role responsible for two things that should never have been separated: how Mews brings products to market, and how Mews understands the market it operates in. You will lead the product marketing team, own the research and customer insights function, and serve as the go-to authority on both disciplines for senior leadership across the business.</p> <p>Mews operates across property management, fintech and payments, guest experience, and marketplace. The right person for this role knows how to build a coherent positioning story across a complex multi-product portfolio – and how to ground that story in real market intelligence, customer insight, and competitive understanding rather than assumption.</p> <h3>RESPONSIBILITIES</h3> <h3>Product marketing strategy</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Define and own product marketing strategy across the Mews portfolio – covering positioning, messaging, and go-to-market execution from launch through adoption and ongoing engagement.</p> </li> <li> <p>Build and govern the global product launch framework so that launches are scalable and repeatable, with clear handoffs between strategy and execution.</p> </li> <li> <p>Own product adoption and post-launch engagement strategy – moving the function beyond launch execution to continuous market thinking that drives usage, retention, and revenue contribution.</p> </li> <li> <p>Partner with Product, Sales, RevOps, and Customer Success to ensure product marketing strategy connects to commercial outcomes and is reflected in how the business goes to market.</p> </li> <li> <p>Own NPS tracking programs and design the measurement framework for product marketing impact, including product attach rates, adoption metrics, and pipeline contribution.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Market research and customer insights</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Own the end-to-end market research function: identifying research opportunities, designing methodology, running studies, synthesising findings, and activating insights across the business.</p> </li> <li> <p>Lead primary and secondary research initiatives that inform strategic, commercial, and product decisions – including competitive analysis, customer behaviour, market sizing, and buyer intelligence.</p> </li> <li> <p>Build competitive intelligence as a structured, ongoing discipline – not a one-off project. Translate competitive signals into positioning decisions, sales enablement, and product roadmap input.</p> </li> <li> <p>Serve as the functional authority on what the market is telling Mews, and translate that into insight narratives that influence senior leadership decisions and business strategy.</p> </li> <li> <p>Work closely with Strategy, Product, RevOps, and Marketing to ensure insights land where decisions get made, not just where they get read.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Team and function leadership</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Lead and develop a team of product marketers, setting clear expectations, building capability, and creating a culture of commercial accountability.</p> </li> <li> <p>Set the operating model for how the team works with AI – determining where AI handles execution tasks and where human judgment is irreplaceable, and building team-level standards accordingly.</p> </li> <li> <p>Serve as the senior leadership go-to on product marketing and market intelligence – the person any executive can trust for a well-grounded, commercially-connected answer.</p> </li> <li> <p>Represent product marketing and research in executive forums, contributing to annual planning and portfolio prioritisation decisions.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>REQUIREMENTS</h3> <h3>Professional knowledge and experience</h3> <ul> <li> <p>10+ years in B2B SaaS marketing, with the majority of that time in product marketing – not demand generation, not agency, not brand-only roles.</p> </li> <li> <p>Has held a Director, Senior Director, or Head of Product Marketing title, or a broader marketing leadership title that included ownership of the product marketing function.</p> </li> <li> <p>Proven track record managing and developing a multi-person product marketing team, including hiring, coaching, and performance management.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience owning or significantly contributing to a market research or customer insights function – primary research methodology, competitive intelligence programs, or voice-of-customer work.</p> </li> <li> <p>Deep understanding of B2B SaaS go-to-market strategy: positioning, messaging architecture, pricing and packaging alignment, sales enablement, and lifecycle marketing.</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience building or significantly reshaping a product marketing function – not just managing an inherited one.</p> </li> <li> <p>Has operated in a lean, fast-moving environment such as a scale-up, growth-stage, or pre-IPO company. Experience only in large enterprise environments with unlimited resources is unlikely to be a strong fit.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>Skills and capabilities</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Owns GTM strategy end-to-end – from initial positioning through post-launch adoption and continuous market engagement. Experience limited to launch execution is not sufficient.</p> </li> <li> <p>Connects product marketing directly to revenue outcomes. Can articulate how their work has influenced pipeline, product attach rates, adoption, or retention – not just campaign outputs.</p> </li> <li> <p>Translates research into business decisions – not just insight reports. Has a track record of research that changed a strategic or commercial direction.</p> </li> <li> <p>Multi-functional marketing experience beyond product marketing, for example content, SEO, digital, demand generation, or go-to-market strategy.</p> </li> <li> <p>Metrics-driven. Comfortable defining and owning the measurement framework for both product marketing impact and research quality.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong senior stakeholder communication. Able to influence executive decisions, present with authority, and earn trust through substance rather than seniority alone.</p> </li> <li> <p>Publicly visible in the product marketing or insights community – speaker, writer, or recognised contributor to the discipline. Not a requirement, but a meaningful differentiator.</p> </li> </ul> <h3>AI fluency</h3> <p>AI is changing the product marketing function in a way that is more structural than any other recent technology shift. A significant part of this role is deciding what that means for the team at Mews – what AI handles, what stays human, and how to build a team that operates at a higher strategic level as execution work is automated.</p> <p>We expect this person to: use AI tools deliberately and with criteria; describe specific examples of AI changing how they or their team works strategically; have a point of view on where the product marketing function is heading as AI matures; and build team-level standards for AI use, including how to review and quality-control AI-assisted outputs before they reach senior stakeholders or customers.</p> <h3>NICE TO HAVE</h3> <ul> <li> <p>Fintech, payments, or financial services product marketing experience.</p> </li> <li> <p>Hospitality, travel tech, or hotel SaaS background.</p> </li> <li> <p>Both fintech and hospitality in one profile is the strongest possible combination for this role.</p> </li> <li> <p>Global market experience.</p> </li> <li> This is where security meets innovation at enterprise scale. As a security engineer, applications at WRITER, you'll be building the security foundations that protect the AI systems powering some of the world's most recognizable brands. This isn't about saying "no"—it's about finding creative ways to say "yes, and here's how we do it securely." You'll tackle challenges that most security engineers never encounter: securing AI agents, protecting training data pipelines, and designing controls for systems that didn't exist a few years ago.

This role is hybrid from our London office, reporting to the head of security engineering.

  • Build security into the DNA of our AI platform by conducting threat modeling sessions with product teams, designing secure architectures for new features, and ensuring security considerations shape product decisions from day one—not after the fact

  • Own and evolve our application security program including establish and maintain SAST/DAST scanning in CI/CD pipelines, conducting security code reviews for critical changes, and building automation that catches vulnerabilities before they reach production

  • Partner with engineering teams to establish and champion secure coding standards, creating reusable security patterns and libraries that make it easier for developers to build securely by default

  • Design and recommend security features and products that help secure customer environments. You are the advocate and the vision for how we protect and secure customers..

  • Integrate and leverage AI agents to help increase velocity for the security team and the overarching engineering org to ensure that we are proactive in minimizing risk while we build products

  • Lead security assessments and penetration testing of WRITER's applications, AI services, and APIs, identifying vulnerabilities across our tech stack and working collaboratively with teams to remediate issues at scale

  • Design and implement security controls for protecting data pipelines, model training environments, and customer-facing AI agents

  • Stay ahead of emerging threats in the AI/ML security landscape, researching attack vectors specific to LLMs and generative AI, and proactively building defenses against novel risks

This is a hybrid position, based out of our New York City or London hubs. You'll report to our director of engineering. 🦸🏻‍♀️ What you'll do Technical Breadth across disciplines. Bring deep focus to one problem at a time, with the breadth to move between SRE, DevOps, Infrastructure, and Platform work over a quarter or two as the leverage shifts. This is not a thrash-every-week role — most of the time you're heads-down on one substantial initiative (the on-call posture, the release pipeline, the multi-region Terraform layout, the internal platform surface). Cross-layer fluency is what lets you pick the right next initiative; it isn't a weekly context-switch. Simplicity / via negativa. Challenge the status quo and remove toil before adding features — automate operational tasks and infrastructure management with Python or Go, reject tools that don't fit the problem, and treat manual on-call work as a defect to be designed out, not a status quo to be staffed up. Breadth across the stack. Design scalable, fault-tolerant infrastructure across AWS (preferred), GCP, and Azure, working fluently across Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, and the supporting cloud and AI tooling that backs WRITER's high-traffic platform. AI in workflow. Run agents in your daily loop — Claude Code, Droid, Codex, internal skills — to investigate incidents, draft Terraform / Helm changes, write runbooks, scaffold tooling, and review PRs. Build the agentic setup as a collective surface: humans and digital teammates working as one team, with shared skills, shared context, and shared on-call workflows. Encode recurring infra tasks as internal skills any teammate (human or agent) can pick up and run, so the team's throughput compounds — not just your own. Debugging fluency. Lead incident response, post-mortems, and root-cause analyses — trace failures to the underlying problem (never the symptom), apply the learning back into the architecture, and prevent the same incident from happening twice. Non-technical End-to-end ownership. Own the reliability, performance, and efficiency of WRITER's core services end-to-end — define and uphold the SLOs and error budgets, carry the on-call pager, and stand behind the outcome metric, not just the system you shipped. Strategic vs. tactical balance. Balance this week's critical work with the 6–12-month platform direction — ship the on-call-driving fix today while shaping the multi-year observability, cost, and reliability investments that move WRITER's enterprise customers. Cross-functional collaboration. Operate at the seams with product, security, and engineering peers — provide expert guidance on system design for reliability, performance, and scalability from conception through launch, Connect the infra agenda to product and revenue context, and disagree with evidence, not volume. ⭐️ What you need Technical Track record. 5+ years of experience in infrastructure engineering, DevOps, or a similar role focused on building and operating large-scale, high-availability production systems at a high-growth product company. Breadth. Experience running containerisation in production (a real cluster, not a lab), with experience in Helm and Terraform or Pulumi on at least one major cloud (AWS preferred), plus good proficiency in Python or Go for automation and tooling. AI in workflow. AI is part of how you ship, not a thing you've read about — agentic tooling (Claude Code, Droid, Codex, internal skills) is in your daily loop, you've built or adopted AI-assisted workflows others now use, and you have strong opinions on where it's unreliable. This is a hard requirement, not a bonus. Candidates whose actual daily workflow does not already include AI tooling will not be advanced. First-principles + decision-making . Demonstrated ability to Challenge the status quo, proactively identify systemic weaknesses, and propose innovative solutions to complex reliability problems — reason from constraints and failure modes (not analogy or vendor defaults), name the tradeoff in business terms (reliability vs. velocity, cost vs. blast radius, standardisation vs. one-off), and reject the "best practices" answer when it doesn't fit the problem. Reversibility & blast-radius. Make reversible calls by default — write the rollback before you touch production, work fluently with monitoring and logging stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK or equivalent), and stress the system in safe places so it comes back stronger. Non-technical Cross-functional collaboration. Excellent communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills, with a talent for building strong relationships and Connecting with cross-functional teams — surface non-goals before anyone asks, and partner with product, security, and platform peers as one delivery surface. Autonomy & end-to-end ownership. A strong sense of ownership and accountability, eager to Own mission-critical systems and drive them toward peak performance and unparalleled reliability. At least one 0-to-1 infrastructure build you owned end-to-end, with the outcome metric attached. 🎁 Bonus if you have Software-engineering depth. A software-engineering background, not only config and scripting — you've designed, built, and shipped non-trivial production code (services, libraries, internal frameworks) in Python, Go, or a comparable language, you can read and modify the codebases your infrastructure runs, and you move between infra automation and feature engineering without changing brains. 🍩 Benefits & perks (UK full-time employees): Generous PTO, plus company holidays Comprehensive medical and dental insurance Paid parental leave for all parents (16 weeks) Fertility and family planning support Early-detection cancer testing through Galleri Competitive pension scheme and company contribution Annual work-life stipends for: Wellness stipend for gym, massage/chiropractor, personal training, etc. Learning and development stipend Company-wide off-sites and team off-sites Competitive compensation and company stock options Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Manager - Incentives
description: This role sits within the Onboarding & Incentives pillar of the Rider Growth function at Deliveroo, this pillar owns the journey from the moment an applicant expresses interest through to a fully habituated, retained rider. We collaborate closely with Product, Data Science, Regional Operations, Rider Marketing and the Retention team to secure and retain a high-quality fleet. We are seeking a Senior Manager to own three of the core engines behind our rider supply strategy: incentives, performance tracking, and target setting with scope to own wider areas of responsibility as these solutions are productionised. You will have overall accountability of our rider referral program from strategy to execution. You’ll partner closely with the Retention & Resurrection team on retention incentives, ensuring incentive spend across the rider lifecycle is efficient, well-targeted, and joined up. As part of this, you’ll design the governance frameworks needed to ensure all incentives across referrals, retention, resurrection and activation are operating efficiently and tests are designed robustly. You will also own performance tracking of rider hours end-to-end, partnering with teams across acquisition, conversion, activation, and retention to understand the forecast and actuals behind their initiatives, and working with Data Science to attribute causality to that work – giving senior stakeholders an accurate, defensible read on how our supply investments are performing. Finally, you will own our rider applicant target-setting model which is used to determine our rider acquisition forecasts vs top-down targets, working with Science and local Regional Operations teams. Improvements here will ensure we’re able to plan for longer time horizons with greater degrees of accuracy as well as scenario planning with our Rider Marketing team to drive efficiencies in cost per applicant. What we’re looking for Analytical Rigor : You are highly comfortable building and defending forecasting, target-setting, and attribution models, and can translate complex data into clear, actionable recommendations. Ownership & Follow-Through : You take full accountability for the incentives and reporting you own, proactively flagging risks to plan and driving fixes end-to-end. Cross-Functional Collaboration : You work effectively across Data Science, Regional Operations, Retention & Resurrection, and Rider Marketing to align on shared goals and targets. Stakeholder Communication : You can distil complex performance and target-setting narratives into clear, credible updates for senior stakeholders. What you'll be doing Referral & Reactivation Incentives : Own the end-to-end strategy, performance, and budget for rider referral and reactivation incentive programmes, continuously testing and iterating to improve efficiency. Retention Incentive Partnership : Partner closely with the Retention & Resurrection team on retention incentives, ensuring a joined-up approach to incentive spend across the rider lifecycle. Rider Hours Performance Tracking : Own tracking of rider hours performance, partnering with teams across acquisition, conversion, activation, and retention to understand the forecast and actuals behind their initiatives. Partner Operations Manager

The Global Merchant Excellence team

The Merchant excellence team supports accountable for supporting restaurant and retail partners across all markets with key onboarding and lifecycle tasks, acting as their operational support team once they’re live on the platform.

The team:

  • Acts as the sole point of contact for self‑serve partners after they “graduate” from early‑life onboarding, working closely with New Partner Experience and Account Management teams.

Operationally, most day‑to‑day volume is handled by third‑party vendors aligned by language and market, with in‑house L2 teams owning complex queries, escalations, and performance management across markets.

In this role you'll be involved in these key areas:

  1. Managing channel, queue and team leader/ agent performance across our in-house teams in Manchester, UK and Milan, Italy.

  2. Identifying trends in performance and conducting root cause analysis (e.g. Team Leader/agent productivity) to drive improved performance.

  3. Helping define new metrics, targets and best practices to drive improvements in Merchant experience (e.g. first touch resolution)

  4. Present market performance updates and strategic implications to executive leadership.

  5. Identify Operational efficiencies that can be gained through automation and process improvements.

 

What you’ll be doing

Drive technical design and architecture decisions, considering scalability, reliability, maintainability, and long-term product needs. Own systems and initiatives end-to-end, from early discovery and design through implementation, rollout, production operations, and iteration. Collaboration: We work closely across engineering, product, design, data, and operations. Senior engineers are expected to help drive alignment when problems span multiple teams or areas. Pragmatism: We value simple and maintainable solutions that create business impact without unnecessary complexity. Nice to Have Experience in one or more of the following areas would be a plus: Merchant-facing or internal operational tools. Analytics, recommendations, or decisioning systems. Grocery, retail, restaurants, logistics, or marketplace technology. Integrations with external business systems. Kafka or other streaming technologies. Cloud infrastructure such as AWS, Kubernetes, or Docker. Why Join Us? You'll work on products that directly affect how merchants interact with Wolt Deliveroo and DoorDash across Europe. 📍This open role is based in our tech hubs in London.

What You'll Do

As a Senior Fullstack Engineer, you'll own complex product and technical problems across the merchant experience, from problem definition through design, implementation, production, and ongoing evolution.

You'll:

  • Design, build, and operate production systems across backend services and user-facing applications.

  • Lead technically complex initiatives across areas such as merchant onboarding, analytics, recommendations, menu and order management, integrations, or merchant-facing tools.

  • Translate ambiguous business and merchant problems into scalable, pragmatic technical solutions.

  • Drive technical design and architecture decisions, considering scalability, reliability, maintainability, and long-term product needs.

  • Own systems and initiatives end-to-end, from early discovery and design through implementation, rollout, production operations, and iteration.

  • Collaborate closely with product managers, designers, operations, and engineers across teams to align on solutions and delivery.

  • Support and mentor other engineers through design discussions, code reviews, knowledge sharing, and technical guidance.

  • Use AI-assisted development tools effectively to increase engineering velocity, while maintaining strong judgment around correctness, security, maintainability, and quality.

  • Work comfortably outside your primary area of expertise when needed to solve problems end-to-end.

 

How We Work

  • Ownership: Senior engineers take responsibility not only for implementation, but also for understanding the problem, shaping the solution, and ensuring it works successfully in production.

  • Collaboration: We work closely across engineering, product, design, data, and operations. Senior engineers are expected to help drive alignment when problems span multiple teams or areas.

  • Pragmatism: We value simple and maintainable solutions that create business impact without unnecessary complexity.

  • Flexibility: We care more about solving the problem than strict frontend or backend boundaries.

Our Tech Stack

Our backend services primarily use Go and Kotlin, while our frontend applications use technologies such as TypeScript and React.

We also work with technologies including Kafka, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, AWS, Kubernetes, Docker, gRPC, and modern cloud infrastructure.

Our Humble Expectations

We're looking for engineers who have:

  • An AI-first mindset, with strong experience leveraging modern AI tools alongside solid engineering principles to solve problems end-to-end, independently of any specific technology stack.

  • Strong experience designing, building, and operating production software at scale in backend, frontend, or fullstack environments.

  • Experience owning complex features, services, or technical initiatives from problem definition through production and ongoing operation.

  • Strong understanding of system design, APIs, databases, distributed systems, testing, observability, and production reliability.

  • Experience making technical and architectural decisions where there are multiple valid approaches and meaningful trade-offs.

  • A track record of helping other engineers grow through mentoring, technical guidance, code reviews, or knowledge sharing.

  • Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical decisions clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Experience with a modern backend language such as Go, Kotlin, Java, and/or modern frontend technologies such as TypeScript and React.

 

You do not need to be equally strong in frontend and backend. We welcome different balances of experience. You might be primarily a backend engineer who is comfortable making frontend changes when needed, or a frontend-focused engineer who is happy to work with APIs and backend services.

What matters most is that you are comfortable working across boundaries to deliver the right solution.

Nice to Have

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be a plus:

  • Merchant-facing or internal operational tools.

  • Analytics, recommendations, or decisioning systems.

  • Grocery, retail, restaurants, logistics, or marketplace technology.

  • Integrations with external business systems.

  • Kafka or other streaming technologies.

  • Cloud infrastructure such as AWS, Kubernetes, or Docker.

Why Join Us?

You'll work on products that directly affect how merchants interact with Wolt Deliveroo and DoorDash across Europe.

The scope is broad and close to the business, giving you the opportunity to work on meaningful problems across different parts of the merchant journey while developing your skills across the stack.

Defence/SC Clearance Requirements:

SC clearance is required for our customer facing teams. You do not need active SC clearance as we will undertake checks upon you joining, but you must be eligible to pass SC clearance. DV clearance may be required for certain roles, so the ability/willingness to pass DV clearance is advantageous but not essential.

About Cloudscaler

Cloudscaler is a rapidly growing cloud consultancy. We partner with ambitious enterprise and public sector customers to design, build, operate, and support secure, governed cloud platforms that meet the highest regulatory and industry standards.

We are scaling deliberately. Our revenue ambition depends on deploying the right people onto the right work quickly, and on making disciplined use of our capacity. This role is central to that.

The opportunity

This is a new role at the heart of how Cloudscaler resources delivery. You will own the day-to-day matching of our people to client work across our enterprise and growth accounts, and you will build and run a pool of trusted associates that gives us flexible capacity when we need it.

The role turns two of our core operating policies, the Bench Management Policy and the Utilisation & Time Recording Policy, into everyday practice. You will work alongside Engine Room leadership to keep bench colleagues productively deployed, and you will bring an AI-first mindset to a set of tasks that are currently manual. The ambition is a faster, fairer, more transparent resourcing process, run with less administrative overhead.

You will report to the Chief Consulting Officer and work closely with Engagement Managers, Delivery Managers, the Engine Room, the CRO function, and People operations. This is a build role. You will shape the process, not just follow it.

Responsibilities and outcomes

Resource matching and assignment

  • Own resource assignments across enterprise and growth client engagements, from incoming demand through to confirmed placement and mobilisation.

  • Match people to work against a rounded set of criteria: skills, experience, career progression goals, team preferences, client need, and personal asks such as location, industry, and preferred way of working.

  • Balance competing priorities fairly and transparently, holding the tension between billable utilisation and colleagues’ development and wellbeing.

  • Maintain an accurate, forward-looking view of who is available when, working from confirmed end dates and pipeline signals.

  • Flag capacity constraints and skills gaps to leadership early, with enough notice to act.

Bench management and utilisation

  • Support the application of the Bench Management Policy and the Utilisation & Time Recording Policy in day-to-day resourcing decisions.

  • Work alongside Engine Room leadership to suggest bench assignments, keeping colleagues on creditable internal work orders or Small Projects rather than idle bench time.

  • Feed the monthly bench report by keeping resourcing data clean and current across Timely and our HRIS, and support the move from a manual report to an automated one.

  • Help keep non-billable bench time within the agreed RAG thresholds, and give an early warning when capacity and pipeline are drifting apart.

  • Contribute to the weekly Engine Room checkpoint so available work and upcoming priorities are visible and mobilisation stays fast.

Associate pool sourcing and management

  • Build, curate, and grow a pool of trusted associates who can be called on for flexible or specialist capacity.

  • Proactively source associates ahead of need, based on recurring skills demand and pipeline, rather than scrambling when a gap appears.

  • Own the associate relationship: onboarding, quality assurance, engagement, and offboarding, so associates are ready to deploy and represent Cloudscaler well.

  • Maintain associate records, availability, rates, and compliance status, and match associates to demand on the same criteria used for permanent colleagues.

  • Work with commercial and People operations on the contractual, rate, and compliance framework for associates, including IR35 status where relevant.

AI and automation

  • Prioritise the use of AI and automation to cut manual effort across resourcing, matching, and reporting.

  • Identify the highest-friction manual tasks and design lighter, tool-supported ways of doing them, in step with the planned automation of the bench report.

  • Help specify and adopt resourcing tooling that gives a single, reliable view of demand, availability, skills, and the associate pool.

  • Champion accurate underlying data. Good matching and good AI both depend on it.

Reporting and stakeholder management

  • Give the Chief Consulting Officer regular, clear management information on availability, assignments, bench position, and associate coverage.

  • Act as the go-to point for Engagement and Delivery Managers seeking to resource an engagement, and set expectations honestly on what is achievable and when.

  • Coordinate with the CRO function so resourcing forecast and the sales pipeline stay aligned.

How success is measured

In the first 90 days you will have taken ownership of resource assignments across the enterprise and growth accounts, established a working associate pool, and mapped the manual tasks ripe for automation. Ongoing success looks like:

  • Faster time-to-assignment for enterprise and growth engagements, with fewer gaps between assignments for colleagues.

  • Onboarding support for new joiners to ensure a positive first experience of a project (whether internal or client facing)

  • Non-billable bench time held within agreed thresholds, with early flags when the position is moving.

  • A dependable associate pool that can be mobilised at short notice for flexible and specialist needs.

  • Measurable reduction in manual effort across matching and reporting, through AI and automation.

  • Trust from colleagues and managers alike that assignments are fair, transparent, and well matched.

Experience

Professional background

  • Proven experience in resource management, staffing, workforce planning, or delivery operations, ideally within a consultancy, professional services, or technology environment.

  • A track record of matching people to work against multiple, sometimes competing, criteria.

  • Experience building or managing an associate, contractor, or freelance network is a strong advantage.

  • Comfortable holding the commercial tension between billable utilisation and investment in people.

Skills and approach

  • Genuinely AI-first. You reach for automation to remove manual work and can help specify and adopt the right tooling.

  • Highly organised, with strong attention to data accuracy and a calm approach to competing demands.

  • A clear, direct communicator who can set honest expectations and have straightforward conversations about capacity and priorities.

  • Confident working with data and MI, and with systems such as time recording and HR tools.

  • Collaborative and trusted, able to work across delivery, commercial, and People functions.

Desirable

  • Familiarity with cloud consultancy delivery and the roles involved, from Project and Engagement Managers through to Cloud Engineers, Consultants, and Architects.

  • Awareness of public sector delivery and security clearance requirements, and how these affect who can be placed on which work.

  • Exposure to IR35 and associated contractor compliance considerations.

  • Experience introducing or improving resourcing tooling and automation.

Why Cloudscaler

Cloudscaler is scaling rapidly and deliberately. Getting resourcing right is one of the biggest levers we have, and this role owns it. You will have genuine ownership of a new function, the freedom to design how it works, and the mandate to bring AI to bear on work that has always been manual. You will be joining a company that values integrity, community, and mastery, and that backs its people to build things properly.

Benefits

  • Discretionary security clearance bonus for those holding certain clearance

  • Periodic offer of share options schemes

  • 25 days’ annual leave

  • 5 additional days per year towards training, certifications, or charity work

  • Option to buy additional annual leave up to 5 days per year

  • Public holidays opt-out scheme, the option to work on public holidays creating the flexibility to enjoy your time off when it suits you

  • Certifications and training expensed
